title: Meetings: The Basics
objective: Learn the basic language of business meetings — starting, talking and ending.
grammarDetail: Present Simple for schedules.  Use it for routines and timetables. Example:  The meeting starts at 10. We meet every Monday.

title: Writing a Simple Professional Email
objective: Learn how to write a short, clear professional email in English.
grammarDetail: Polite requests.  Use  could you  and  please  to sound polite. Example:  Could you please send the report? Could you confirm by Friday?

title: Phone Calls and Video Calls
objective: Learn basic phrases for phone and video calls — starting, speaking and ending.
grammarDetail: Introductions.  Use  this is / speaking  on the phone. Example:  Hello, this is Emily. Emily speaking.

title: A Short Business Presentation
objective: Learn the basic structure and phrases of a short business presentation.
grammarDetail: Signposting.  Use simple words to guide the audience:  First, then, after that, finally.  Example:  First, I will show the numbers. Then, I will explain the results.

title: Negotiation: Asking for What You Need
objective: Learn simple negotiation phrases for small daily requests at work.
grammarDetail: Can / could.  Use  could  to sound more polite. Example:  Can I have more time? Could we meet tomorrow instead?

title: Making Decisions at Work
objective: Learn basic phrases to share opinions and make simple decisions.
grammarDetail: I think / I believe.  Use them to share opinions. Example:  I think option A is better. I believe we need more information.

title: Problems and Solutions
objective: Describe small work problems and propose simple solutions.
grammarDetail: Countable / uncountable.   Information, advice, work  are uncountable — no plural. Example:  I need some information. Can I give you a piece of advice?

title: Project Basics: Tasks and Deadlines
grammar: Prepositions of time — by, on, in
objective: Learn the basic language of simple projects — tasks, people and deadlines.
grammarDetail: By / on / in for time.  Use  by  for deadlines,  on  for days,  in  for months or years. Example:  Please finish by Friday. The meeting is on Monday. We will launch in March.

title: Time Management: One Day at Work
objective: Describe a typical working day and talk about priorities and time.
grammarDetail: Daily routine verbs.  Use Present Simple:  I start, I check, I finish, I take a break, I reply.  Add frequency adverbs:  always, usually, often, sometimes, never.

title: Networking and Small Talk
objective: Learn simple phrases for small talk at work events and coffee breaks.
grammarDetail: Question forms.  Use  how, what, where  to open small talk. Example:  How are you? What do you do? Where are you from? How was your weekend?

title: Giving and Getting Feedback
objective: Learn simple phrases to give and receive daily feedback at work.
grammarDetail: Positive adjectives.  Build a small bank:  clear, strong, good, helpful, friendly, calm, kind, honest.  Example:  That was a very clear presentation.

title: Reporting and Status Updates
objective: Share simple status updates at work in a clear and organised way.
grammarDetail: Present Perfect with just / already / yet.  Example:  I have just finished the report. I have already sent the email. I haven't spoken to the client yet.

title: Writing a Short Business Report
objective: Learn to write a short, structured business report at beginner level.
grammarDetail: Linkers.  Connect ideas with  and  (add),  but  (contrast),  so  (result). Example:  Sales are up, but costs are up too. So, profit is the same.

title: Difficult Conversations at Work
grammar: I feel / I think — opening phrases
objective: Use soft, calm phrases for small difficult conversations.
grammarDetail: I feel / I think.  Open difficult topics with  I :  I feel worried about this. I think we need to talk.  It is softer than  you -sentences.

title: Managing Up: Talking to Your Boss
objective: Learn simple phrases to share ideas, problems and plans with a manager.
grammarDetail: Would like.  More polite than  want . Example:  I would like to share a small problem. I would like to ask for your advice.

title: Working with People from Other Countries
objective: Learn simple phrases to work with colleagues from different cultures.
grammarDetail: More / less.  Example:  In some cultures, people are more direct. In others, they are less formal at meetings.

title: Numbers, Data and Simple Charts
objective: Learn to read and say numbers, percentages and simple charts in English.
grammarDetail: Big numbers.  Practise saying:  one hundred, a thousand, a million. Fifteen percent, twenty-five percent.  English speakers say  "point"  for decimals:  "three point five percent".

title: Change at Work: Adapting to New Things
objective: Talk about small changes at work and how we adapt to them.
grammarDetail: Going to.  Use for decided plans:  We are going to use a new tool. I am going to try it this week.

title: Taking Care of Customers and Clients
grammar: Helping verbs — let me / can I
objective: Learn basic phrases to welcome and help clients in a friendly way.
grammarDetail: Let me / Can I.  Offer help in a friendly way:  Let me check that for you. Can I help you with anything else?

title: Ethics and Doing the Right Thing
objective: Learn simple words to talk about honesty, ethics and doing the right thing at work.
grammarDetail: Should / shouldn't.  Use for advice and moral rules:  You should tell the truth. You shouldn't hide mistakes.
